prerequisites: Introduction to Mechanical Design (INTRODUCCIÓN AL DISEÑO MECÁNICO)

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialization, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the competencies of the degree, including notions of the latest advances.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Capacity for engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; to appropriately choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods and to correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Capacity for engineering analysis: The ability to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems in their specialization; to appropriately choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods; to recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialization that meet established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as to select and apply appropriate project methods.
Engineering projects: Ability to project using advanced knowledge from their engineering specialization.

Research and innovation: Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult, and critically use databases and other sources of information, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialization.
Research and innovation: Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialization.
Research and innovation: Ability and skill to design and carry out experimental research, interpret results, and draw conclusions in their field of study.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, design, and research and their limitations in their specialization.
Practical application of engineering: Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects, and conduct research specific to their specialization.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology, and engineering processes and their limitations in their specialization.
Practical application of engineering: Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialization.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial implications of engineering practice.
Judgment formulation: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialization, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions within the field of engineering and with society in general.

Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers as well as with people from other disciplines.
Continuous training: Ability to recognize the need for one's own continuous training and to undertake this activity throughout one's professional life independently.
Continuous training: Ability to stay up-to-date with developments in science and technology.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, arguing and justifying each one, and making correct use of language, in writing.

teaching_methods: Project-Based Learning (POPBLs) activities, including development, writing and presentation of reports and audiovisual material (individual or team)
Individual study and work, tests, exams, and control points
Lectures by the professor in participatory classes, covering concepts and procedures
Practical work in workshops and/or laboratories (individual or team)

assessment_methods.method: Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, technical presentation and defense
Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices
Observation of student participation and attitude in the proposed training activities

assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation and feedback are provided. For the evaluation of competence RGM316, the minimum grade for both the report and the individual test to be averaged is 5. There are no recovery mechanisms for the individual written and oral tests for competence RGM316. A feedback session is provided before the defense for competence RGM316.
